rules_text:
You can use the following mechanics in campaigns that center 
on curses, queens, and oracles.
CURSES
A creature afflicted with a magical curse gains the Cursed 
condition. The Cursed condition can only be cleared by 
magic from a spell, ritual, magic item, location, supernatural 
occurrence, higher power, or some combination of these 
options. Discovering how to end a curse often requires 
research, which might prompt the PCs to undergo a quest for 
additional information or help from an NPC.
TRANSFORMING ADVERSARIES
“Transform” is a special action that enables an adversary to 
shift between multiple stat blocks. By default, the adversary 
has a primary stat block that includes stats and features 
available to the adversary regardless of their active form. 
While in a particular form, the adversary has access to the 
stats and features contained in that form’s stat block and their 
primary stat block. Unless noted otherwise, the adversary 
tracks HP and Stress on their primary stat block regardless of 
their active form.
BUILDING VILLAINS 
COLLABORATIVELY
You can build a campaign villain collaboratively using the 
following process.
Prior to your session zero, write approximately 40 prompts, 
each in the form of a question about the villain. For example, 
you might ask about the villain’s background, demeanor, 
motives, or reputation. Write each prompt on an index card or 
slip of paper. For inspiration, see the Reign of the Weredragon 
Villain Builder sheet in Hope & Fear or available online at  
daggerheart.com/downloads.
During session zero (and prior to character creation) randomly 
select about 15 of your prepared prompts and place them in 
the center of the table so that everyone can reach them but no 
one can read them.
Starting with the person to your left, each player draws one of 
the pre-selected prompts and reads it aloud, then chooses one 
of the following options:
• The active player can answer the prompt. Other players 
can ask follow-up questions, though the active player can 
choose not to answer them.
• The active player can remove the prompt from play and 
draw a new prompt.
• The active player can pass the prompt to another player, 
who likewise chooses to answer, remove, or pass it.
When there are no more follow-up questions to a prompt, play 
passes to the left. Continue in this manner until all prompts at 
the center of the table have been answered or removed. Then 
proceed to character creation.
200
Daggerheart SRD
